chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kumaydani narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family said to Gabriel: Advise me. He said: O Muhammad! Live as much as you want, for you will die. Love whatever you want, for you will be separated from it. Do whatever you want, for you will encounter it. The honor of the believer is his night prayer, and his glory is his keeping his tongue/hands from the faults of people.
ai.seo_question: What are the three pieces of advice Gabriel gave to the Prophet Muhammad regarding life and death?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, presents a concise triad of existential realities—death, separation, and accountability—that frame the Prophet’s interaction with Gabriel, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly attachments. It subsequently grounds spiritual nobility in two practical pillars: *Qiyam al-Layl* (night prayer), reflecting the Shia emphasis on devotion and vigilance, and *Kaff al-Lisan* (restraint from slandering others), highlighting social ethics as a marker of true faith. This synthesis of metaphysical awareness and ethical conduct is central to Shia moral theology, linking individual piety with communal harmony.
